So if by chance we had the unfortunate or misfortune that on May 18 that the majority of our voters voted no, we could potentially go to a contingency budget if the board did not opt to go out for another vote. In a contingency budget that requires the district to levy no more than the previous year's levy that would require the district to make cuts of approximately $1.4 million and would result in a budget increase of only $384,000 from the 2021 budget. In a contingent budget, there would be no new equipment purchases, no community use of our facilities, and no capital improvements unless it was an emergent situation. Other necessary cuts would also certainly have deep impacts on staffing and student programs, curriculum, professional development initiatives, and other purchases that we have spoken of making throughout this budget process.
